title: AI Agent Human Approval: How to Add It (2026 Guide)
summary: AI agent human approval differs by platform. Compare how each tool pauses risky actions, asks the right person, and logs approval decisions.
body_markdown:
## Zapier, Make and Power Automate approval options


Of the three, Power Automate ships the most finished approval step. Zapier gives you a dedicated pause action, and Make asks you to build the pause yourself from a webhook and a message.


### Zapier approvals


To pause a run in Zapier, you add its Human in the Loop tool as a step in a Zap. Its Request Approval action stops the run, sends the request to a named person, and resumes only after they answer.


**Put the exact action in the message body** ("Refund this customer, this order, this amount") and the approver can judge it in a glance. Leave it as a generic "Approve?" and you've built a button people press without reading.


If your team already lives in Zapier's app library and wants the pause without writing logic, it suits you. Check its pricing page for which plan includes the tool, because I won't state a tier from memory.


Anyone who needs the approval record elsewhere has to export it, because it lives inside Zapier's run history.


### Make approvals


In Make, the pause is something you assemble. A common pattern is two scenarios. The first sends the proposed action to the approver in Slack or email with a link, then stops.


Then a second scenario starts from a custom webhook that the link calls, reads the approve or reject value, and carries out the action.


You have to add the safeguards yourself. **Nothing stops someone clicking the link twice** , so build a check that the request is still pending. Nothing logs who approved unless you write that into a data store or sheet.


If you're comfortable with branching and routers and want the approval to look exactly the way you designed it, Make suits you. Confirm on Make's own documentation whether a native approval module has been added for your plan, since I haven't verified one.


### Microsoft Power Automate


In Power Automate the approvals are built in. The Start and wait for an approval action sends a request to chosen people by email, Teams or the Approvals app, and the flow holds until someone responds.


You pick the approval type, such as approve or reject, or first to respond versus everyone must approve.


Put the amount, the customer and the reason in the Details field, which takes formatted text. The outcome and the approver's comments come back as outputs, and the response is recorded in the Approvals app, so the audit trail comes mostly for free.


It suits organisations already on Microsoft 365, where approvers sit in Teams all day. Licensing depends on your Microsoft agreement, so check what your plan includes before committing.
